accuracy.evidence: Pauling electronegativities O 3.44 and C 2.55 give Cδ+ / Oδ−. IUPAC naming checked: propanal (no locant for aldehydes), propanone and butanone (no locant needed), pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one (lowest locant from the end nearest C=O), methanal and ethanal; no 2-carbon ketone exists. General formula CₙH₂ₙO for saturated straight-chain aldehydes and ketones. Nucleophilic attack at the carbonyl carbon (CN⁻ addition) and the non-polar C=C contrast match AQA/OCR A-level specifications, Chemguide and the IUPAC Blue Book rule P-64.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented A-level slips: δ− on carbon (first prediction, place() feedback, challenge 'pol'), reading CH₃COCH₃ as an aldehyde because of the letters C-H-O (sort step, m4, challenge 'form'), propan-1-al and ethanone (m2, p5, build-step prediction, 'small' tag), numbering from the wrong end such as pentan-4-one (m3, 'num' tag), same formula meaning same compound (slide prediction, m1) and nucleophiles bonding to O (nuc prediction, m5, 'nuc' tag).

lab_distinct.evidence: Mechanics are specific to carbonyls: dragging δ+/δ− charge tags onto C and O, tapping carbons to slide a C=O along a chain with live name, family and formula, a chain-length builder that only accepts the named target, a condensed-formula sorter for –CHO vs –CO–, and a drag of :CN⁻ onto C=O versus C=C. It shares no step with the functional-group reagent bench, the radical chain or benzene labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover each rule by acting: wrong charge placement explains electronegativity; sliding the O shows end = aldehyde, middle = ketone, and that carbon 3 is still propanal; the builder shows a 2-carbon chain cannot hold a ketone and names what the target needs; mis-sorts explain CHO vs CO; wrong nucleophile targets explain repulsion by δ− O and the non-polar C=C.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong answers that the task disproves: carbon as δ− 'because it has more bonds', same formula = same compound, ethanone exists, and CN⁻ bonding to oxygen.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven items with rotating answer positions; each distractor carries a tag (pol, fam, num, small, form, nuc) with its own explanation, the answer is shown after a miss, and the canvas keeps a drawn propanal with the polarity rule on screen.

readability.evidence: Learner and adult text pass the repo's Flesch-Kincaid limits (6.5 and 9.5). Terms (carbonyl, electronegativity, δ+, nucleophile) are defined with an example on first use; lab prompts are one or two short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a rule or fact the lab tests; the adult text lists concrete mistakes and a quick check. Lab copy is instructions and feedback only, and no gate filler phrase matches.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots: large C and O atoms with charge tags of 56 px height, chain carbons spaced to the screen width with tap areas spanning the whole column, + C / − C pads of 56×50 px, two sort bins over a wide formula card, and a 24 px nucleophile ball. Buttons below the canvas are at least 44 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every gesture has a button twin: 'δ+ on C' etc., 'C=O on C1–C3', '+ carbon' / '− carbon', 'Aldehyde' / 'Ketone' and 'To carbonyl C/O' / 'To alkene C', with full aria-labels. The canvas aria-label reports charges, current name, family and formula, build target, bin counts or the attack result. axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
